items.title: No completed-test outcome in the current dashboard
items.whyItMatters: Orders overstate completion, especially for urine albumin (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Define the outcome as both tests resulted within the window from laboratory results in the extract.

items.title: Rollout schedule may relate to performance
items.whyItMatters: If early practices differ systematically, the comparison is biased.
items.opportunity: Compare pre-rollout trends and baseline adherence between waves and adjust for baseline.

items.title: Duplicate testing of patients seen in hospital
items.whyItMatters: Feedback has increased duplicate tests elsewhere.
items.opportunity: Measure tests within 30 days of a hospital result as a balancing measure.

items.title: People in deprived areas and of working age
items.whyItMatters: They complete ordered tests least often.
items.opportunity: Report completion by deprivation quintile and age band.

items.title: The landmark trial is an unchecked lead
items.whyItMatters: It is presented as definitive but has no retrieval or identity check.
items.opportunity: Search for it by identifier before anyone cites it; do not plan around its effect size.

errorsFound: The first gaps reply was prose, not JSON, and relied on the unchecked landmark lead; it was not applied.
reevaluation: The cohort comparison stands, with completed tests as the outcome, baseline adjustment, a balancing measure and equity reporting.
summary: Five gaps; outcome definition and schedule bias are high severity.
